$comment: The master menu of testable flows. Each id EXACTLY matches a key in `procol test/src/master/registry.ts`, so the Executor can look the flow up and run it. Mirrors the registry (source of truth). Run `npm run check:catalog` to confirm they are still in sync.

flows.name: PR → Event
flows.description: Takes an existing Purchase Request and turns it into a sourcing event, carrying the PR's line items across. Confirms the new event group is saved in the database.

flows.name: Create RFP + RFQ event (2-stage)
flows.description: Creates a two-stage event: a technical RFP stage and a pricing RFQ stage. Confirms both stages were saved in the database.

flows.name: Create RFP-only event
flows.description: Creates a single technical (RFP) stage event and confirms it in the database.

flows.name: Create RFQ-only event
flows.description: Creates a single pricing (RFQ) stage event and confirms it in the database.

flows.name: Create rank-based auction event
flows.description: Creates an auction event ranked by position and confirms it in the database.

flows.name: Create price-based auction event
flows.description: Creates an auction event ranked by price and confirms it in the database.

flows.name: Create RFP + Auction event (2-stage)
flows.description: Creates a two-stage event: a technical RFP stage followed by an auction stage. Confirms both stages in the database.

flows.name: Create → surrogate bid → award proposal
flows.description: Full happy-path: create an event, place a bid on the vendor's behalf (surrogate), then open an award proposal. This is the closest flow to 'create and award an RFQ event'.

flows.name: Version an event group (F2)
flows.description: Creates an event and then makes a new version of it. Confirms the versioned trades exist.

flows.name: Convert RFQ stage to auction (F5)
flows.description: Creates an event then converts its pricing (RFQ) stage into an auction. Confirms the auction stage is active.

flows.name: Create BOQ-based event
flows.description: Downloads a Bill-of-Quantities Excel template, parses its sections and line items, and creates a BOQ event group. Confirms the BOQ flag is saved in the database.

flows.name: Create a product category
flows.description: Creates a product category and confirms it in the database.

flows.name: Create a product
flows.description: Creates a category, a family under it, then a product, and confirms the product in the database.

flows.name: Create a location (buyer hub)
flows.description: Creates a delivery/buying location and confirms it in the database.

flows.name: Create a team
flows.description: Creates a purchasing team and confirms it in the database.

flows.name: Create a user (grant permissions via team)
flows.description: Creates a team, then creates a user assigned to that team (team membership is how permissions are granted). Confirms the user and team in the database. NOTE: the phone field has strict validation — it must be a valid Indian mobile like 98xxxxxxxx with phone_prefix '+91'. This is the input the 'try to break the inputs' request targets.

notableInputs.rule: A valid phone is exactly 10 digits with phone_prefix '+91'. The frontend form enforces digits-only + length 10 (validateCountryPhone, utils/index.js:195-203).
notableInputs.knownQuirk: Server-side validation on POST /users/create_user checks LENGTH (rejects 9 or 11 digits with 422 'Invalid phone number') but does NOT check that the characters are digits — a 10-character value containing letters (e.g. '9876543ABC') is accepted (HTTP 200). The API is more lenient than the UI, letting a malformed phone into the users table. Strong target for data-validation testing.

flows.name: Fetch the client's vendor list
flows.description: Reads the client's list of vendors. Always available (read-only).
